title: Same three-step bedtime
subtitle: Wash, one book, lights out at the time you picked
description: Do the same three steps: wash, one book, lights out at the clock time you picked. Done when the lights are out.

title: Make the room dark and cool
subtitle: Curtains closed, extra lights off
description: Close the curtains and turn off extra lights before the last book. Done when the room is dark and cool.

title: Screens off 60 minutes before bed
subtitle: TV, tablet, and phones leave the room
description: Turn off TV, tablet, and phones 60 minutes before the bedtime you picked. Done when the screens are off and out of the room.

title: 5 minutes outside after waking
subtitle: Open the curtains, then step out together
description: Open the curtains and step outside together for 5 minutes after waking. Done when you have both been outside.

title: Keep wake-up time reasonably consistent
subtitle: Within about an hour of the usual time
description: Wake them within about an hour of the time you picked, including slower mornings. Done when they are up in that window.

title: Bathroom stop before lights out
subtitle: Last trip, then into bed
description: Take one bathroom trip after the last drink and before lights out. Done when they are back in bed.

title: Talk about sleep without a lecture
subtitle: Ask how they feel, then stop
description: Ask one question about how last night felt, then stop. No rules speech. Done when you asked and listened.

title: Serve one fruit or vegetable with the meal
subtitle: On the plate or table. Eating is optional.
description: Put one fruit or vegetable with the main meal. Done when it is available, whether or not they eat it.

title: Let them decide how much to eat
subtitle: You choose what is served. They choose the amount.
description: Serve the meal, then let them decide whether and how much to eat. No pressure for “one more bite.” Done when the meal ended without a serving fight.

title: Eat one meal together
subtitle: Same table. Phones away.
description: Sit down for one meal in the same place with phones away. They can leave food. Done when you ate together.

title: Include a protein food at breakfast
subtitle: Eggs, beans, nut butter, yogurt, or leftovers
description: Put one protein food on the breakfast table: eggs, beans, nut butter, yogurt, cheese, or leftovers. Done when it was served.

title: Offer water with meals instead of sugary drinks
subtitle: Juice, soda, and sweet tea stay off the table
description: Put water at the meal and leave sugary drinks off the table. Done when water was the drink served.

title: Include one high-fiber food today
subtitle: Fruit, beans, oats, whole grains, or vegetables
description: Serve one high-fiber food today: fruit, beans, oats, whole grains, or vegetables. Done when it was on the table.

title: Eat without commenting on their body
subtitle: No “you look” or “you need to eat more”
description: During meals, skip comments about their body, weight, or how much they “should” eat. Done when the meal ended without those comments.

title: Don’t label foods good or bad
subtitle: Talk about how often, not morality
description: If food comes up, talk about how often you eat it instead of calling it good or bad. Done when you used that language once today.

title: Try one unfamiliar food without pressure
subtitle: Seeing, touching, or tasting all count
description: Put one unfamiliar food on the table. Seeing, touching, or tasting it counts. No “just try it.” Done when it was offered without pressure.

title: Eat slowly enough to notice fullness
subtitle: Pause once during the meal
description: Pause once during the meal and ask if their belly feels hungry, okay, or full. Done when you paused and they answered.

title: Get outside today
subtitle: 20 to 30 minutes together
description: Spend at least 20 minutes outdoors together: yard, walk, park, or errand on foot. Done when the time outside is finished.

title: Move for an hour across the day
subtitle: Walk, play, sports, dance — it all counts
description: Add up about an hour of movement across the day: walk, run, playground, cycling, or dancing. Done when the hour is in.

variants.2-4y: Add up about an hour of movement: playground, dancing, or chasing you down the hall. Short bursts count. Done when the hour is in.
variants.5-8y: Add up about an hour of movement: walk, playground, bike, or sport. Done when the hour is in.
variants.9-12y: Get about an hour of movement across the day: sport, bike, walk, or play. Done when the hour is in.
variants.13-18y: Get about an hour of movement: walk, lift, sport, or a bike ride. It does not have to be a workout. Done when the hour is in.

title: Take a family walk after dinner
subtitle: 10 to 15 minutes together
description: Walk together for 10 to 15 minutes after dinner. Stroller or scooter is fine. Done when you are back inside.

title: Practice one physical skill
subtitle: Throw, catch, balance, jump, climb, ride, or kick
description: Practice one physical skill for a few minutes: throw, catch, balance, jump, climb, ride, or kick. Done when you practiced once.

title: Let them play freely outside
subtitle: You stay nearby. You do not run the game.
description: Give them unstructured outdoor play without directing the activity. Stay nearby for safety. Done when they played without your plan.

title: Move for 10 minutes before homework
subtitle: Walk, jump, or shoot hoops first
description: Give 10 minutes of movement before they sit down for homework. Done when the 10 minutes finished and they sat down.

title: 15 minutes of hard play
subtitle: Run, bike, or playground before dinner
description: Get 15 minutes of hard play before dinner: run, bike, jump, or a playground. Done when the 15 minutes of movement are finished.

title: Brush teeth morning and night
subtitle: Two minutes each time. You help as needed.
description: Brush morning and night for two minutes. For younger kids, you do most of it. For older kids, you check. Done when both brushes happened.

variants.2-4y: You brush their teeth morning and night for two minutes. They can hold the brush after. Done when both brushes happened.
variants.5-8y: They brush; you finish the two minutes morning and night. Done when both brushes happened.
variants.9-12y: They brush morning and night for two minutes. You check once. Done when both brushes happened.
variants.13-18y: They brush morning and night for two minutes. A reminder is enough. Done when both brushes happened.

title: Wash hands when coming home
subtitle: Soap and water before snacks or toys
description: Wash hands with soap when you walk in, before snacks or toys. Done when hands are washed.

title: Wash hands before eating
subtitle: Soap, rinse, then sit down
description: Wash hands with soap before the meal starts. Done when everyone who is eating has washed.

title: Wash hands after the bathroom
subtitle: Soap and water before they leave the sink
description: Wash hands with soap after using the bathroom. Done when they washed before leaving the sink.

title: Put on sunscreen before a long time outside
subtitle: Face, neck, and arms before you go
description: Put sunscreen on face, neck, and arms before extended outdoor time. Done when it is on before you leave.

title: Bring a water bottle to school
subtitle: Fill it the night before or at breakfast
description: Fill a water bottle and put it with the bag they take to school. Done when it is packed.

title: Change into clean clothes after heavy activity
subtitle: Sweaty clothes go in the hamper
description: After sports or heavy play, change into clean clothes and put the sweaty ones in the hamper. Done when they changed.

title: Teach one body-care skill
subtitle: Hair, nails, deodorant, skin, or period care
description: Teach or review one body-care skill: hair washing, nails, deodorant, skin care, or period supplies. Done when you practiced it once.

title: Take three slow breaths together
subtitle: In through the nose, out through the mouth
description: Take three slow breaths together: in through the nose, out through the mouth. Done when you finished the third breath.

title: Rate the feeling 1 to 5
subtitle: 1 is small. 5 is huge.
description: Ask them to rate the feeling from 1 to 5. You can rate yours too. Done when a number was said out loud.

title: Name the feeling before reacting
subtitle: One word first. Then the next step.
description: Before anyone fixes or argues, name the feeling in one word. Done when the feeling was named first.

title: Name the feeling out loud
subtitle: “You’re frustrated.” Then wait.
description: When they are upset, say the feeling in one short line: “You’re frustrated.” Then wait. Done when you named it once.

title: Ask what their body feels like
subtitle: Tight chest, hot face, or fast heart
description: Ask “What does your body feel like?” Offer tight chest, hot face, or fast heart if they need choices. Done when they answered.

variants.2-4y: Ask “Is your tummy tight, or is your face hot?” Point to the body part if they need help. Done when they pointed or answered.
variants.5-8y: Ask “What does your body feel like?” Offer tight chest, hot face, or fast heart. Done when they answered.
variants.9-12y: Ask where they feel it in their body before you solve it. Done when they named a body signal.
variants.13-18y: Ask what they notice in their body — jaw, chest, stomach — before you offer a fix. Done when they named one signal.

title: Pick a calm-down strategy
subtitle: Water, breathing, quiet corner, movement, or a cuddle
description: Let them pick one: water, breathing, a quiet corner, movement, or a cuddle. Done when they chose and started it.

title: Say what you need
subtitle: “I’m angry because ___. I need ___.”
description: Help them finish “I’m upset because ___ . I need ___ .” You can model it first. Done when the two blanks were filled.

title: Practice a calm-down while they are already calm
subtitle: Do not wait for a meltdown to teach it
description: Practice one calm-down while everyone is already okay: breaths, a quiet spot, or a squeeze. Done when you practiced once.

title: Notice one difficult emotion they handled
subtitle: Name the feeling and what they did
description: Name one hard feeling they handled today and what they did. Done when they heard the sentence.

title: Stay calm and present until the feeling settles
subtitle: Listen before you solve it
description: Stay nearby, keep your voice even, and listen before you solve it. Done when you stayed until their body settled or they were ready to talk.

title: Offer movement when emotions are overflowing
subtitle: A walk, jump, or stretch — they can say no
description: When feelings overflow, offer movement: a walk, jump, or stretch. They can refuse. Done when you offered it once.

title: Ask how a story character feels
subtitle: One question during the bedtime book
description: During the bedtime book, ask “How do you think they feel?” Done when you asked once and heard their answer.

title: 7 minutes at breakfast, phone down
subtitle: Phone face-down the whole time
description: Sit together for 7 minutes at breakfast with your phone face-down. Talk, eat, or just be in the same room. Done when the 7 minutes are finished.

title: Reconnect for 7 minutes after school
subtitle: Listen before chores or screens
description: When they walk in, spend 7 undivided minutes together before snacks turn into screens. Listen, sit, or play. Phone stays away.

title: End with 7 connected minutes
subtitle: Cuddle, read, or talk. No screens.
description: Spend 7 undivided minutes at bedtime. Cuddle, read, or share the day. Done when the 7 minutes are up and screens stayed off.

title: Daily check-in
subtitle: One question. Then listen.
description: Ask today’s check-in question and listen without fixing. Done when you asked and heard their answer.
prompts: What was the best part of your day?
What do you wish had gone differently?
What are you looking forward to tomorrow?

title: Have one conversation without giving advice
subtitle: Ask, then stay quiet
description: Have one conversation and do not give advice. Ask a question, then listen. Done when you finished without a fix.

title: Ask what they are excited about
subtitle: One thing. No follow-up lecture.
description: Ask what they are excited about right now. Listen to the answer. Done when you asked and did not turn it into a lesson.

title: One step, then 10 seconds
subtitle: Say it once. Wait before you repeat.
description: Give one instruction, like “Shoes by the door.” Do not repeat it for 10 seconds. Done when you said one step and waited.

title: Give a 5-minute warning
subtitle: Name the next thing before you switch
description: Before play or a screen ends, say “Five more minutes, then bath.” Done when you gave the warning before the switch.

title: Let one natural consequence happen
subtitle: You do not rescue the forgotten item
description: Let one natural consequence stand, like a forgotten item staying forgotten. Stay kind. Done when you did not rescue it.

title: Give them one job they own
subtitle: Set the table, feed a pet, or take out trash
description: Give them one job they finish on their own: set the table, feed a pet, or take out trash. Done when that job is finished.

title: Let them try the small problem first
subtitle: Wait, then one hint if they are stuck
description: When a small problem shows up, let them try first. Count to 20, then offer one hint if they are stuck. Done when they tried before you took over.

title: Let them dress themselves
subtitle: You lay out options. They put them on.
description: Let them dress themselves. Lay out two options if they need help choosing. Done when they put the clothes on, even if they are mismatched.

title: Let them clean up their own spill
subtitle: Hand them a cloth. Help only if needed.
description: Hand them a cloth and let them clean the spill. Help only if they cannot finish. Done when they started the cleanup.

title: Let them ask the question
subtitle: At a store, restaurant, or school office
description: Let them order or ask the question themselves at a store, restaurant, or office. You stand nearby. Done when they asked.

title: Put dirty clothes in the hamper
subtitle: The clothes they took off today
description: Put today’s dirty clothes in the hamper. Done when they are in the basket, not on the floor.

title: Clean up before starting something new
subtitle: Toys, dishes, or the homework spot
description: Put away the last activity before the next one starts. Done when the last thing is cleared.

title: Help prepare one part of the meal
subtitle: Wash, stir, pour, or set one thing
description: Let them prepare one part of the meal: wash, stir, pour, or set the table. Done when that part is finished.

title: Give them control over one small decision
subtitle: Clothes, snack, activity, or book
description: Let them choose one small thing today: clothes, snack, activity, or book. Done when their choice stood.

title: Teach one household skill
subtitle: Folding, sweeping, dishes, or laundry
description: Teach or practice one household skill: folding, sweeping, dishes, cooking, or laundry. Done when they did one step themselves.

title: Everyone helps reset the room for five minutes
subtitle: Timer on. Everyone picks up.
description: Set a five-minute timer and have everyone reset the room. Done when the timer ends and people helped.

title: Child clears their own plate
subtitle: To the sink or the counter
description: They carry their plate to the sink or counter after the meal. Done when the plate is there.

title: Put away one thing they used
subtitle: A cup, toy, charger, or jacket
description: They put away one thing they used today. Done when it is back where it belongs.

title: Thank someone for helping
subtitle: Name the person and what they did
description: Thank someone in the house for a specific help. Done when the thank-you named the person and the action.

title: Let them manage one responsibility independently
subtitle: You do not hover. You check later if needed.
description: Hand them one responsibility and let them manage it without hovering. Done when you stayed out of it until it was finished.

title: Discuss money once this week
subtitle: A purchase, a budget, or a job
description: Have one short money talk this week: a purchase, a budget, or earning. Done when you talked once without a lecture.

title: Read together for 10 minutes
subtitle: One book or a few pages. You can take turns.
description: Read aloud together for 10 minutes. They can follow along or take a page. Done when the 10 minutes are up.

title: Ask one “Why do you think…?” question
subtitle: Then wait for their idea
description: Ask one “Why do you think…?” question about something you saw or read. Done when you waited for their idea.

title: Spend 10 minutes creating something
subtitle: Draw, build, write, or make music
description: Spend 10 minutes making something: draw, build, write, or make music. Done when the 10 minutes are up.

title: Let boredom happen
subtitle: No immediate screen when they say “I’m bored”
description: When they say they are bored, do not hand over a screen. Wait or offer a non-screen option. Done when boredom got time to sit.

title: Solve one everyday problem together
subtitle: A stuck zipper, a lost shoe, a recipe step
description: Solve one everyday problem together out loud. Done when you worked the problem instead of you doing it alone.

title: Count, cook, or build during normal life
subtitle: Numbers, steps, or pieces in a real task
description: Use counting, cooking, or building inside a normal task. Done when they did one of those during the task.

title: Ask a question before giving the answer
subtitle: “What do you think?” first
description: When they ask something you know, ask what they think first. Then share the answer if they still want it. Done when you asked first.

title: Visit or explore something new this week
subtitle: A street, shop, park, library, or trail
description: Go somewhere slightly new this week: a street, shop, park, library, or trail. Done when you went once.

title: Prepare tomorrow tonight
subtitle: Clothes, bag, and shoes — age decides who does which
description: Get tomorrow ready tonight. Ages 2–4: clothes and shoes out. Ages 5–8: pack the bag together. Ages 9+: they pack; you glance. Done when clothes and bag are ready.

variants.2-4y: Put tomorrow’s clothes and shoes out together. Done when both are ready.
variants.5-8y: Pack the bag together: water, folder, and one thing they choose. Clothes out. Done when bag and clothes are ready.
variants.9-12y: They pack the bag. You glance. Clothes ready. Done when bag and clothes are ready.
variants.13-18y: They get tomorrow ready. You do not repack it. Done when they say it is ready.

title: Set the homework spot first
subtitle: Chair, pencil, and paper out before they sit
description: Before homework starts, put the chair, pencil, and paper in the same spot. Done when the spot is ready and they sit down.

title: Start with a 5-minute timer
subtitle: One small task, then a break
description: Set a 5-minute timer for the first homework or chore. When it rings, they can pause. Done when the timer ran once.

title: Ask someone a question today
subtitle: A classmate, sibling, or neighbor
description: Ask someone a real question and wait for the answer. Done when they asked once.

title: Give one genuine compliment
subtitle: About something specific they noticed
description: Give one specific compliment about something they actually noticed. Done when the sentence was said.

title: Invite someone to join
subtitle: Play, lunch, or a walk
description: Invite someone to join play, lunch, or a walk. Done when the invite was said.

title: Take turns without being reminded
subtitle: One game or one toy
description: Practice taking turns in one game or with one toy without a reminder from you. Done when a turn was given.

title: Practice saying “No, thank you”
subtitle: A food, a hug, or an extra activity
description: Practice “No, thank you” for a food, hug, or extra activity. Done when they said it once and it was respected.

title: Look for someone left out
subtitle: Then say hi or make space
description: Notice someone left out and say hi or make space. Done when they looked and did one small thing.

title: Repair after hurting someone
subtitle: Name what happened. Then make it right.
description: After they hurt someone, help them name what happened and make it right. Sorry alone is not enough. Done when the repair was said.

title: Ask before touching or borrowing
subtitle: Wait for a yes
description: Ask before hugging, grabbing, or borrowing. Wait for a yes. Done when they asked first.

title: Practice disagreeing without insults
subtitle: “I see it differently” counts
description: Practice disagreeing without insults. “I see it differently” counts. Done when a disagreement stayed respectful.

title: Tell someone when a boundary is crossed
subtitle: A short line is enough
description: Practice telling someone a boundary was crossed, in a short line. Done when they said it once.

title: Do one helpful thing without being asked
subtitle: A door, a bag, or a leftover chore
description: Do one helpful thing nobody asked for: a door, a bag, or a leftover chore. Done when they did it.

title: Talk about one friendship moment today
subtitle: What happened, and how they felt
description: Talk about one friendship moment: what happened and how they think the other person felt. Done when you talked it through.

title: Know one friend they are spending time with
subtitle: A name and how they know them
description: Learn or confirm one friend they are spending time with: a name and how they know them. Done when you know both.

title: Talk about relationships without a lecture
subtitle: Ask what they think. Then listen.
description: Talk about a relationship topic and ask what they think before you share yours. Done when you listened first.

title: Praise effort or strategy once today
subtitle: Or say “I noticed you…” about the try
description: Praise a specific effort or strategy, or say “I noticed you…” about the try. Skip “you’re so smart.” Done when they heard the sentence.

title: Leave one small mistake unfixed
subtitle: Crooked, messy, or unfinished is allowed
description: Leave one small mistake unfixed: crooked, messy, or unfinished. Done when you did not redo it.

title: Ask “What did you learn?” after something hard
subtitle: After a miss, not only after a win
description: After something hard, ask what they learned. Done when they answered and you did not jump to a lecture.

title: Name one thing they are getting better at
subtitle: A skill, not a grade
description: Name one thing they are getting better at, even if it is still messy. Done when they heard it.

title: Let them teach you something
subtitle: A game, a fact, or a move
description: Let them teach you a game, a fact, or a move. Follow their instructions. Done when they taught and you tried.

title: Name a brave try, not only a win
subtitle: The attempt is the point
description: Name one brave try, whether or not it worked. Done when they heard that the attempt counted.

title: Ask them to make one decision
subtitle: How to handle a small problem
description: Ask them to decide how to handle one small problem. Stand by their choice if it is safe. Done when they chose.

title: Make the meal device-free for everyone
subtitle: Every phone and tablet leaves the table
description: Keep phones and tablets off the table for the meal, including yours. Done when the meal stayed device-free.

title: Decide the stopping point before the screen starts
subtitle: An episode, a level, or a clock time
description: Before a show or game starts, agree on the stopping point: an episode, a level, or a clock time. Done when you named it out loud first.

title: Charge phones outside the bedroom
subtitle: Plug them in before lights out
description: Plug phones and tablets in outside the bedroom before lights out. Done when they are charging in the other room.

title: No screens for the first 30 minutes home
subtitle: Snack, play, or talk first
description: Keep TV, tablets, and phones off for the first 30 minutes after they get home. Done when 30 minutes passed without a screen.

title: Set a timer before the game starts
subtitle: They can see the clock
description: Set a visible timer before a game starts and stop when it rings. Done when the timer was on before play began.

title: Talk about one thing happening online
subtitle: A video, chat, or trend — no raid
description: Talk about one thing happening online. Ask, then listen. Done when you talked without taking the phone.

title: Ask before hugs or tickling
subtitle: Wait for a yes. A no stands.
description: Ask before hugs or tickling and wait for a yes. A no stands. Done when you asked first.

title: Stop as soon as they say stop
subtitle: Roughhousing and tickling count
description: If they say stop during play, stop immediately. Done when you stopped the first time they said it.

title: Use the correct names for body parts
subtitle: Say the real words once today
description: Use the correct names for body parts at least once today. Done when the real words were used.

title: Name one trusted adult
subtitle: Who they could tell if something felt wrong
description: Ask who they could tell if something made them uncomfortable. Name one trusted adult together. Done when a name was said.

title: Practice “No, stop, I don’t like that”
subtitle: Say it once. You take it seriously.
description: Practice “No, stop, I don’t like that” out loud. You take it seriously. Done when they said the line once.

title: Never keep unsafe secrets
subtitle: Surprises are fine. Secrets that feel bad are not.
description: Talk through the difference: surprises are okay, secrets that feel bad are not. Done when you said both out loud.

title: Check in before going somewhere
subtitle: They tell you where they are going
description: They tell you where they are going before they leave. Done when you heard the place and they left.

title: Seatbelt check before driving
subtitle: Click, then the car moves
description: Check that every seatbelt is on before the car moves. Done when you checked and then drove.

title: Helmet on before bike or scooter
subtitle: Strapped, then they roll
description: Put a helmet on before a bike, scooter, or skateboard. Done when it is strapped before they roll.

title: Don’t share passwords with friends
subtitle: A phone, game, or school login
description: Remind them not to share passwords with friends. Done when you said it and they repeated the rule.

title: Pause before sharing a photo
subtitle: Ask: would I want this saved forever?
description: Before they send a photo, pause and ask if they would want it saved. Done when you paused once.

title: Tell an adult about a disturbing message
subtitle: They are not in trouble for showing you
description: Tell them they can show you a disturbing message and will not be in trouble. Done when you said that out loud.

title: Talk about consent and boundaries
subtitle: One short, judgment-free conversation
description: Have one short talk about consent and boundaries without judgment. Done when you talked and they could respond.

title: Talk about alcohol, vaping, or drugs before they come up
subtitle: Facts first. No scare speech.
description: Have one calm talk about alcohol, vaping, or drugs before they are in the room. Done when you talked once this week.

title: Answer one body question honestly
subtitle: Short, true, and without teasing
description: Answer one body question honestly and without teasing. Done when you answered in plain words.

title: Normalize one puberty change
subtitle: Name it as expected, not weird
description: Name one puberty change as expected. Done when you said it in a matter-of-fact way.

title: Check that hygiene supplies are stocked
subtitle: Soap, deodorant, pads, or razor
description: Check that soap, deodorant, pads, or a razor is stocked. Done when you looked and restocked if needed.

title: Talk about deodorant without a speech
subtitle: Body odor is a body fact
description: Talk about deodorant or body odor in a matter-of-fact way. Done when you mentioned it without embarrassment.

title: Treat periods as a normal topic
subtitle: For any child in the house
description: Talk about periods as a normal body process, for any child. Done when you mentioned it without whispering.

title: Let them ask an awkward question without teasing
subtitle: Thank them for asking
description: When an awkward question comes, thank them for asking and skip the tease. Done when the question got a straight answer.

title: Use correct anatomical terms
subtitle: The real words, said calmly
description: Use correct anatomical terms when the body comes up. Done when the real words were used calmly.

title: Talk about body changes without commenting on looks
subtitle: No “you look grown” or rating
description: Talk about body changes without commenting on attractiveness. Done when the talk stayed about function, not looks.

title: Remind them bodies develop at different speeds
subtitle: Early and late are both normal
description: Remind them that bodies develop at different speeds. Done when you said early and late are both normal.

title: Put the phone away when they start talking
subtitle: Face-down or in another room
description: When they start telling you something, put the phone away. Done when you looked at them for the whole share.

title: Get down to their level before correcting
subtitle: Knees or a chair. Then the words.
description: Get down to their level before you correct them. Then say the words. Done when your face was near theirs first.

title: Connect before correcting
subtitle: A hand, a name, or one kind line first
description: Before a correction, connect first: a hand, their name, or one kind line. Done when the connect came first.

title: Give one instruction without yelling
subtitle: A normal voice. One step.
description: Give one instruction in a normal voice. Done when you said it once without yelling.

title: Replace one threat with a clear boundary
subtitle: What happens, said calmly
description: Swap one threat for a clear boundary: what happens next, said calmly. Done when you used the boundary instead.

title: Follow through on one boundary calmly
subtitle: You do the thing you said
description: Follow through on one boundary you already stated, without a lecture. Done when you did the thing you said.

title: Don’t repeat yourself five times
subtitle: Say it once. Then wait or help the start.
description: Say the instruction once. Then wait or help them start. Done when you did not stack five repeats.

title: Catch them doing something right
subtitle: Name the action while it is happening
description: Catch them doing something right and name the action. Done when they heard it in the moment.

title: Ask instead of assume
subtitle: One curious question before the story in your head
description: Ask one curious question before you assume why they did something. Done when you asked first.

title: Repair one moment out loud
subtitle: “I was sharp. I’m sorry.”
description: If you snapped today, say “I was sharp earlier. I’m sorry.” Done when they heard the sentence.

title: Say “I love you” with nothing attached
subtitle: No “if you…” and no grade
description: Say “I love you” with nothing attached to it. Done when they heard it without a condition.

title: Spend 10 minutes letting them lead
subtitle: They pick. You follow.
description: Let them pick the game or talk and follow for 10 minutes. Done when the 10 minutes are up.

title: Ask before offering a solution
subtitle: “Do you want ideas, or just a listen?”
description: Ask “Do you want ideas, or just a listen?” before you solve it. Done when you asked and followed their answer.

title: Give them privacy
subtitle: Knock. Stay out of the bag and the phone.
description: Give privacy for their room or bag: knock, and stay out of the phone. Done when you respected that line once today.

title: Offer two acceptable choices
subtitle: “Shoes first or jacket first?”
description: Give two options you can live with, like “Shoes first or jacket first?” Done when you offered two choices and stood by either.

title: Say what they can do
subtitle: “Walking feet inside,” not “Don’t run.”
description: Swap one “don’t” for what they can do: “Walking feet inside.” Done when you said the can-do line.

title: Give the consequence once
subtitle: Say it. Then do it. No extra speeches.
description: State the consequence one time, then follow it. No repeats. Done when you said it once and followed through.

title: Validate the feeling and hold the no
subtitle: “I know you’re angry. The answer is still no.”
description: Name the feeling, then hold the limit: “I know you’re angry. The answer is still no.” Done when both parts were said.

title: Don’t renegotiate after the boundary is set
subtitle: The first no stays the no
description: After you set a boundary, do not bargain it away. Done when the first no stood.

title: Notice cooperation immediately
subtitle: Name it while they are still doing it
description: When they cooperate, name it in the moment. Done when they heard it while still doing the thing.

title: They turn the screen off when the timer rings
subtitle: You set it. They press stop.
description: They turn the TV or game off when the timer rings. You do not grab the remote first. Done when they turned it off.

title: Use “When → Then”
subtitle: “When your shoes are on, then we leave.”
description: Use one When-Then: “When your shoes are on, then we leave.” Done when you used that frame once.

title: Keep the consequence related to the behavior
subtitle: The fix matches what happened
description: Pick a consequence that matches the behavior, not a random punishment. Done when the follow-through was related.

title: Don’t punish while you are angry
subtitle: Pause. Then decide.
description: If you are angry, pause before a consequence. Decide when your voice is even. Done when you waited.

title: Give one respectful redo
subtitle: “Try saying that again respectfully.”
description: Offer one redo: “Try saying that again respectfully.” Done when you offered the redo and heard a second try.

title: Check tomorrow’s school plan once
subtitle: Assignments or the calendar, together
description: Look at tomorrow’s assignments or calendar together once. Done when you both saw the plan.

title: Break one large task into three steps
subtitle: Write the three. Then start number one.
description: Pick one big task and write three steps. Start step one only. Done when the three steps are written.

title: Start with the easiest next action
subtitle: “Open the document,” not “finish the project.”
description: Name the smallest next action, like “Open the document.” Done when they started that small step.

title: Use a visible checklist
subtitle: Three boxes they can see and tick
description: Put a three-item checklist where they can see it. Tick as they go. Done when the list was visible before they started.

title: Work, then a short break
subtitle: A timer for work. Then a timer for rest.
description: Set a work timer, then a short break. Ages 5–8: 10 minutes. Older: 20. Done when both timers ran.

variants.5-8y: Work for 10 minutes, then a 5-minute break. Done when both timers ran.
variants.9-12y: Work for 20 minutes, then a 5-minute break. Done when both timers ran.
variants.13-18y: Work for 25 minutes, then a short break they choose. Done when both parts happened.

title: Let them estimate how long it will take
subtitle: They guess. Then you start the clock.
description: Ask how many minutes the task will take. Start a clock. Done when they guessed and work started.

title: Pack finished work immediately
subtitle: Folder, then bag, before they stand up
description: As soon as work is done, it goes in the folder and bag. Done when it is packed before they leave the spot.

title: Create a distraction parking spot
subtitle: Phone and toys leave the work table
description: Park the phone and toys away from the work table before they start. Done when the table is clear.

title: Ask them to tell you the first step
subtitle: “What’s the first thing you’ll do?”
description: Ask “What’s the first thing you’ll do?” Wait for their answer before you plan it. Done when they said the first step.

title: Name the worry
subtitle: “What is your brain telling you might happen?”
description: Ask what their brain is telling them might happen. Write or say the worry. Done when the worry was named.

title: Separate worry from fact
subtitle: What we know vs what we are guessing
description: Sort the worry: what we know, and what we are guessing. Done when both columns were said.

title: Do one small brave step
subtitle: To the door is enough. Not the whole thing.
description: Pick one small brave step, like walking to the classroom door. Done when they did that step.

title: Don’t immediately remove every discomfort
subtitle: Stay nearby. Don’t cancel the hard thing.
description: Stay nearby, but do not cancel the hard thing the first time they protest. Done when you stayed and the thing still happened.

title: Practice the situation before it happens
subtitle: Walk through it once while they are calm
description: Rehearse the hard moment once while they are calm: drop-off, the test, the talk. Done when you walked through it.

title: Use a predictable goodbye
subtitle: Same three steps. Then you leave.
description: Use the same three goodbye steps, then leave. No extra laps. Done when you did the three steps and left.

title: Ask: comfort or a plan?
subtitle: Let them pick before you jump in
description: Ask “Do you want comfort, or help making a plan?” Then do that. Done when you asked and followed their pick.

title: Name the bravery after they did it
subtitle: Not “See, there was nothing to worry about.”
description: After a hard thing, say “You were nervous and you still did it.” Done when they heard that line.

title: Don’t force an immediate apology
subtitle: Cool-off first. Then repair.
description: Do not force “sorry” in the heat. Wait, then help them repair. Done when you skipped the forced apology.

title: Hear each child separately before judging
subtitle: One at a time. Then you decide.
description: Hear each child once before you pick a side. Done when both had a turn.

title: Describe the problem without a villain
subtitle: “You both want the same toy.”
description: Name the problem without a villain: “You both want the same toy.” Done when you said the problem, not who is bad.

title: Let each child suggest one solution
subtitle: Then pick one you can live with
description: Each child suggests one fix. You pick one that is safe. Done when both offered an idea.

title: Don’t compare siblings
subtitle: No “Why can’t you be more like…”
description: Skip any comparison to a sibling today. Done when the day ended without one.

title: Give each child a short block of individual attention
subtitle: Ten minutes. One child. No sharing.
description: Give one child ten undivided minutes. The other gets a turn another time. Done when the ten minutes were just for them.

title: Notice teamwork between siblings
subtitle: Name the moment they helped each other
description: Name one moment they helped each other. Done when they heard the sentence.

title: Fill their water bottle after waking
subtitle: First drink ready before the day gets busy
description: Fill a water bottle as soon as they wake so the first drink is ready. Done when the bottle is filled.

title: Let them own one morning step
subtitle: Teeth, clothes, bag, or breakfast setup
description: Pick one part of the morning they do without you taking over: teeth, clothes, bag, or breakfast setup. Done when they finished that step.

title: Preview the morning in three steps
subtitle: Breakfast → shoes → school
description: Say the morning in three steps before it starts: breakfast, shoes, school. Done when they heard the three steps.

title: Get ready before entertainment screens
subtitle: Morning routine first. Screens second.
description: Finish the morning routine before any entertainment screens come on. Done when they were ready first.

title: Name one thing they're looking forward to
subtitle: One thing about today
description: Ask what one thing they are looking forward to today. Done when they named something, even a small one.

title: Have a snack and water before homework or screens
subtitle: Body first, then the next demand
description: Offer a snack and water after school before homework or screens. Done when they had both.

title: Choose how to decompress after school
subtitle: Snack, quiet, movement, talking, or outside
description: Let them choose how to land after school: snack, quiet, movement, talking, or outside. Done when they picked one and did it.

title: Empty today's school bag
subtitle: Papers, lunchbox, and finished work
description: Empty today's bag: papers to the right place, lunchbox to the kitchen, finished work to a parent or shelf. Done when the bag is empty.

title: Finish one small responsibility before leisure
subtitle: Bag, clothes, pet, or dishes — then free time
description: Ask for one small responsibility before leisure: bag away, clothes away, pet, or dishes. Done when that job finished first.

title: Reset their space for 2 minutes
subtitle: Clothes away, cup out, floor clear
description: Reset their space for two minutes: clothes away, cup out, floor clear. Done when the timer ends.

title: Name tomorrow's first important thing
subtitle: One thing they need to remember
description: Ask what the first important thing is tomorrow. Done when they named it out loud.

title: Don't make the last conversation a correction
subtitle: End the night with one warm sentence
description: Before sleep, make the last interaction connection rather than instruction or criticism: “I loved hanging out with you,” “Goodnight, love you,” or something specific from the day. Done when the last sentence was warm.
